segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: [At the time of the Echo Flight shutdown] what was unusual was that several of the missiles were open...for some routine maintenance. I don’t remember why. But, uh, at least two of them were running on diesel power so they were not connected to the power grid. I don’t remember if it was three open or four open [but] it was just routine maintenance. Nothing had happened [to the missiles]. It was just the time of the year for routine maintenance. Um, and the day before, there were maintenance teams out there. They had stayed overnight—

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Do you know how many maintenance teams were out overnight?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: You know, I think it was four. It was the two sites that had diesels running and two others. And when maintenance stays overnight they...stay in a camper...When you have maintenance on the site and they’re going to stay overnight, you have a security team on the site.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Right. (Break. Figel goes into detail about security procedures.)

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: [When] the missiles dropped off alert, I started calling the maintenance people out there on the radio to talk to them. I had the security guard authenticate so I know I’m talking to a security guard and, you know, [I asked] “What’s going on? Is maintenance trying to get into the silo?” [The guard said,] “No, they’re still in the camper.” [So, I said,] “Get ‘em up, I want to talk to them.” Then I tried to tell them what I had was a Channel 9 No-Go. Hastings: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Uh, we did that with the sites that were there, that [had maintenance teams and their guards on site] and I sent Strike Teams to two other sites. There’s no sense sending them where I [already] have a guard and a gun and an authenticate.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Right.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Uh—

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: So far in this narrative, you haven’t mentioned UFOs.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: [Laughs] That’s correct. Um, somewhere along the way, um, one of the maintenance people—cause he didn’t know what was going on any place else either, they have no capability of talking to each other [at different launch sites], in other words, they can talk to the [launch] capsule but they can’t talk to each other—

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Right

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: —unless they were on the radio and no one was using the radio except the security police. And the guy says, “We got a Channel 9 No-Go. It must be a UFO hovering over the site. I think I see one here.” [I said,] “Yeah, right, whatever. What were you drinking?” And he tried to convince me of something and I said, well, I basically, you know, didn’t believe him. [Laughs] I said, you know, we have to get somebody to look at this [No-Go]. [A short time later] one of the Strike Teams that went out, one of the two, claimed that they saw something over the site.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: How did they describe that?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Oh, on radio, [they said,] “There’s this large object hovering over the site!” I’ve always been a non-believer [in UFOs] so I said, “Right, sure you do.” [They responded,] “Yeah! Yeah, we do!” So, [I said,] “There’s two of you there, saying so, so write it down in your report.” [The Strike Team leader] said, “What do you want us to do?” [I said,] “Follow your checklist. Go to the site, open it up, and call me.”

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: What was the demeanor of the guard you were talking to?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Um, you know, I wouldn’t say panicked, or anything [like that]. I was thinking he was yanking my chain more than anything else.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: But he seemed to be serious to you?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: He seemed to be serious and I wasn’t taking him seriously.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Alright. If it was a large object, did he describe the shape of the object?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: He just said a large round object.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Directly over the LF?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Directly over the site. (BREAK. Figel describes hearing from the maintenance man about his opening up the silo, going down into it, and reporting that even though the missile was offline, nothing was visually damaged or otherwise amiss at the site.)

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Did he describe the object leaving the scene?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No. He never said anything about it again. (BREAK. Figel describes telling all the maintenance teams to stay at their sites until relieved, and not to attempt repairs until told to do so, since the missile silos were in effect “crime scenes”.)

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: When you got the first call, well, when the missiles went down, you didn’t have an inkling of an alleged UFO-involvement until you got the report back from the first Strike Team member?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: That’s correct.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: (Actually, the missile maintenance man mentioned seeing the UFO first.)

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay, uh, and only one of the two teams reported seeing an object?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Right.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Uh, did you discuss the report with Mr. Carlson—that you were being told that there was a UFO at one of the sites?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Um, he could hear it, uh, I mean he was sitting right there, two feet away from me—

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: So—

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Whatever I said, he would have heard. (Break. Figel describes going back to Malmstrom with Carlson and being debriefed by “everybody and his brother.”)

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Did any of the conversations back at squadron headquarters, uh, was there any mention of UFOs?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I told them everything everyone told me. No one made any comments or inquiries—

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: So you did mention the report that you got from the Strike Team?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: And no one asked any questions about UFOs per se?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Did they act skeptically or negatively when you mentioned [the Strike Team’s UFO report]?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: They just wrote things down.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: [Laughs] That sounds right. Poker-faced and—

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: [Laughs] Poker-faced and wrote things down. They just said, “Thank you very much. Don’t talk about it.” I didn’t sign anything, I can tell you that. (Break. Hastings describes similar testimony from other missileers who were debriefed at Malmstrom and other Strategic Air Command bases, following UFO-related incidents in the missile fields.)

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: What did Eric [Carlson] have to say [about the shutdown incident]? (Hastings had interviewed Carlson two weeks earlier, on 10/6/08)

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Uh, he said that he couldn’t recall any UFO-involvement in the incident. He couldn’t remember if you had mentioned UFOs, one way or another. His son [James] has now [posted] on a blog, a web log, a couple of lengthy statements in which he defamed Salas, said Salas was a liar, [and said] there was nothing involving UFOs at Echo...

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Did Eric say anything else that was a discontinuity [relative to what I’ve said]?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: ...Well, I [told Eric] that you had [heard from] a guard or a maintenance person that there was an object above the site, which you’ve confirmed today—

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: —And I asked Eric if he remembered any of that, and he said that he did not. And, um, I asked him why his son would have written this scathing, very negative summary, which I will send [to] you, about the event—

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: That will be interesting.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: —calling Salas a liar, and so on and so forth.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Well, I didn’t do that.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Well, I know, but his son, you know, for whatever reason, his son, James Carlson, has got a bug up his nose and said that nothing happened, there were no reports of UFOs, which you told me is incorrect because you got one.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I did!

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Well, according to James, it was all bull and Salas was basically pulling it out of the air. [Eric] Carlson just, he didn’t really want to talk about it, frankly, but he did answer my questions. He just was kind of circumspect. I can’t say that he’s not being truthful when he says he doesn’t remember talking to you about UFOs, but that’s what he told me.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I’m sure we had a long conversation. I mean, I reported everything to him that I heard or was told. I mean, we were together, you know? [Laughs]

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Well, it has been 40 years, so we have to take that into account. [That is, the possibility of faded memories.]
